Independent analytic grouped-site risk and equality derivation
correctness.rationale: Unrestricted quadratic polynomials force the three moment constraints. For any design, group calls by site: exact worst-case bias in absolute value is (a/6)∑_u |u|³|∑_{δ_j=u} w_j|, attained by assigning aligned remainder signs with disjoint smooth cutoffs away from the anchor. The largest variance is b∑_j w_j² and can be realized with that same function. Averaging repeated-site weights leaves this bias invariant and strictly decreases the variance unless already equal; thus it suffices for the lower bound and is necessary for an optimizer. Equation (2) in the proof uses this averaged-design reduction (the expression with ungrouped absolute weights need not bound the risk of a raw mixed-sign repeated-site design). After this reduction, Hölder yields C≥S⁻²; the zero-sum constraint gives sign totals S/2. Separate Cauchy–Schwarz gives variance at least bS²(1/p'+1/q')/4, uniquely minimized in the counts when all n weights are used with the most balanced split. The positive-scalar minimum for odd n occurs at S⁶=a²/(18bk_n), k_n=n/(n²−1), with the stated exact value. Equality in the slope triangle inequality and Hölder forces sign agreement and a common nonzero |δ|=1/S. Thus only the reflected/permuted replicated two-site designs attain the bound, and they satisfy even the quadratic exactness constraint. A cubic realizes the worst bias at these sites. For n=1 the first two moments conflict; the even-budget formula and both n=3 percentages also check.
correctness.replay: Apply the exact grouped-site bias formula, pairwise averaging, and the inequality (1/p'+1/q')/4≥n/(n²−1) at odd n. With S=1/h, minimize a²h⁴/36+bk_n/h² and track weighted Hölder and sign-class equality.
residual_risks: Exactness is only for deterministic nonadaptive linear estimators with independent centered call errors of bounded variance; does not extend here to correlated, adaptive, or nonlinear schemes.
